title: Hardware Problems
drDigitalIntro:
Hardware means the parts you can touch — the screen, the keys, the sockets, the speakers. Software problems you can fix. Most hardware problems you check, then hand over.
• A dark screen: turn the brightness up in Settings first. If it stays dark, plug the charger in and wait a minute — a flat battery looks exactly like a broken computer.
• Keys or mouse not working: push the cable in properly at both ends. If it has no cable, change the batteries.
• No sound: check the volume is up and not muted. Then try headphones. If the headphones work, the speaker is the problem, not the computer.
• Smoke, a burning smell, sparks, or a cracked screen: stop. Unplug it and take it to a repair shop. Do not open it up yourself.
• The safe rule: check the settings and the cables, then restart. If it is still wrong after that, it is time to ask someone who repairs computers.
drDigitalSuccess: You know what to check first when the trouble is the machine itself rather than something on the screen. Most of it turns out to be a cable or a flat battery.
drDigitalHint: Read through the checklist and click Continue when you are ready.
